$comment: WORKING DEFAULT (open design question 12). Pipelines do not use MCP. They call the record endpoint with this contract, as a workload identity that holds the deployment recorder role through a Workload Grant (C42). Document 24, sections 4.5, 4.6 and 9.2; document 23, P05; document 25, sections 7, 8 and 11.4.
description: The record endpoint contract for pipeline record steps. A pipeline has no model choosing tools, so it does not use MCP. It calls one plain HTTPS endpoint with the same contract as record_deployment, and corrections with the same contract as record_deployment_correction. The response body is the same envelope the MCP tool returns.
failSoft: Record steps fail soft (I-189): on any error, timeout or non-2xx status the step writes a warning to the run log and never fails the deployment. A retry with the same idempotencyKey is always safe. Stopping a deployment is the later check step's job (check_change_approval, after D-03), never the record step's.

authentication.holdsRoleThrough: A Workload Grant (C42) per pipeline identity, with a reason, the deciding decision and an expiry (workload-grant-max-days). Workload identity federation, no secret. On Dataverse, an application user that holds the role directly.
notAccepted: Delegated user tokens: people record deployments through record_deployment on MCP or on the page.
Agent identities: they never get a Workload Grant.

idempotency: idempotencyKey in the body is the upsert key of the Deployment Record (unique). The Idempotency-Key header of the Azure binding (document 25, section 12.1) is optional; when sent it must equal idempotencyKey.

statuses.when: A new record was written. data.created is true.
A retry matched the idempotency key, or validateOnly was true. data.created is false. Nothing new was written.
The body does not match the request schema, or a key is not allowed.
No valid app-only token.
The token lacks the Deployment.Record app role, the identity has no valid Workload Grant, or the token is a delegated user token.
A given row ID does not exist, such as changeRequestId.
The idempotency key was reused with a different body.
A configuration rule refused the write, such as a URL that matches a forbidden pattern.
Too many calls. The error carries retryAfterSeconds.
No valid active configuration, or no gate policy row matches. There is no built-in fallback.
